title: A floor NOT gates cannot lower: at least 2N gates for one family, at every size from 3
dek: For the complement of the N by N matching, every fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit on one-a-side inputs needs at least 2N gates, from N = 3. Checked in Lean; at size 5, from our own proof.

body.p: For one family of graphs, the record has a floor that stands even when the circuit may use NOT gates: every such circuit needs at least 2N gates for the graph of size N, from size 3 on. It is checked in Lean. At size 5 it answers one of our own hunts with a no: no circuit of at most 9 gates exists there.

Take a grid of connections between N rows and N columns. Switch on exactly one row and exactly one column, and ask a circuit of gates, each an AND, an OR or a NOT reading at most two wires, to say whether that row and that column are connected. We call these one-a-side inputs. How many gates such a circuit needs is how this project comes at its question.

The graph here is the complement of the matching: row u is joined to every column except column u. With three rows and three columns, row 0 meets columns 1 and 2, row 1 meets columns 0 and 2, and row 2 meets columns 0 and 1. So the circuit must answer one question: are the row and the column that are on different from each other?

body.h: A floor, raised twice in ten minutes

body.p: Late on 25 November three floors for this family came back checked, each a gate higher than the last. At least 2N - 2 gates [L-meta-17177] and at least 2N - 1 gates [L-meta-17185], both from N = 2, were checked at 23:16 UTC, and at least 2N gates, from N = 3, at 23:26 [L-meta-17187]. The fleet files each such statement together with its opposite, so that whichever one is right can be checked; the record marks all three opposites as broken [L-meta-17182, L-meta-17186, L-meta-17192].

At N = 5 the floor says 10 gates. One of our own desk asks had wondered whether 9 might do at that size. That ask is broken on the record [L-meta-17199], and its opposite, that no circuit of at most 9 gates represents the 5 by 5 case, is checked from a proof file of the fleet's own [L-meta-17200]. It is the general floor at one size, checked separately; it adds no further size, and it closes the question the ask had opened.

body.h: What it is and what it is not

body.p: The floor is linear: it grows like 2N, and the circuit has 2N input wires, one for each row and each column. So it says that NOT gates cannot make this family cheap; it does not say the family is hard in the sense that matters most, which would need a floor growing faster than the number of inputs. Most floors on our record are about circuits without NOT gates; this one allows them, which is why it is worth telling.

The other half is a ceiling. Whether some AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most 2N gates represents this family at every size is on the record as a conjecture [L-meta-20790]. If it is checked, the cost of this family with NOT gates allowed is exactly 2N from size 3 on, and the record has a family where NOT gates are allowed and the count is known exactly at every size.
